Ship analytical depth from the audit's Add list:
- Clients tab: cohort retention heatmap, LTV histogram, new-clients-per-month line chart
- Bookings: per-service columns (revenue, avg ticket, no-show%), walk-in vs booked breakdown

## Tasks (execute in order)

### 1. Extend `app/api/reports/clients/route.ts` — depth queries

Add to ClientsBlock:
```ts
interface ClientsBlock {
  // existing KPIs
  totalClients: number
  newClients: number
  returningClients: number
  inactive90d: number
  avgLtvCents: number
  retentionRate: number  // 0..100

  newClientsByMonth: Array<{ month: string; count: number }>  // last 12 months
  cohortRetention: Array<{ cohort: string; cohortSize: number; retentions: number[] }>  // [n1pct, n2pct, n3pct, n4pct, n5pct, n6pct]
  ltvDistribution: Array<{ bucket: string; min: number; max: number | null; count: number }>
}
```

Cohort definition: client cohort = month they were created. Retention[N] = % of cohort that booked a session in calendar month cohort+N (1-indexed). Compute for trailing 12 months of cohorts × 6 follow-on months.

LTV buckets: $0–100, $100–500, $500–1k, $1k–5k, $5k+. Bucket label in display format `"$0–100"`, store min/max in cents (max=null for top bucket).

`newClientsByMonth`: trailing 12 months (or full data range if shorter), each month = count of clients created with `created_at` in that month.

Maintain `{ current, prior? }` shape — these new arrays go in `current` block. Skip in prior unless trivial.

- Y axis: cohort labels (e.g. "Jan 2026", "Feb 2026" ...)

Mobile: horizontal scroll via parent overflow-x-auto; cells stay readable size.

### 3. Build `components/reports/charts/LtvHistogram.tsx` (NEW)
Recharts BarChart, vertical bars. Each bucket = bar with count value. Stone-fill bars with Onyx text. Tooltip shows: `$100–500: 47 clients · 31% of total`.

Sort: ascending by min (so $0-100 leftmost, $5k+ rightmost).

Y-axis: client count. X-axis: bucket label. Brand-locked colors.

### 4. Build `components/reports/charts/NewClientsLine.tsx` (NEW)
Wraps `RechartsAreaChart` (already supports priorData). Pass `data={newClientsByMonth}` mapped to `{ name: month, value: count }`. Pass `priorData` if compare on (compute from prior block if API provides; if not, omit).

Trailing-3-month average is a future enhancement — skip annotation for v1, just plot the line.

### 5. Update `components/reports/ClientsReportClient.tsx`
- Below 4 KPI cards, add 3-section grid: NewClientsLine | CohortHeatmap | LtvHistogram
- Mobile stacks vertically
- Each section in its own Card with shadow-card token
- All respect global `?from`, `?to`, `?compare`
- React Query already keyed properly from Sprint 1

### 6. Extend Bookings — per-service detail + walk-in vs booked

Service ranking now includes:
```ts
interface ServiceRankItem {
  name: string
  count: number
  revenueCents: number    // NEW
  avgTicketCents: number  // NEW: revenueCents / count
  noShowRate: number      // NEW: percent of this service's bookings that no_show'd
```

Walk-in vs booked: use `bookings.source` column (verify it exists; common values are `'walk_in' | 'online' | 'phone' | 'in_person'`). Add to BookingsBlock:
```ts
interface SourceBreakdown {
  walkIn: number
  booked: number  // anything not walk_in
```

If `source` column doesn't exist or isn't reliably populated in the seed, file a follow-up to populate via migration; for now derive walkIn=0 and surface honest empty state in UI when total counts mismatch.

#### 6b. Update `components/reports/BookingsReportClient.tsx`
- Replace flat services list with sortable table — columns: Rank, Name, Bookings, Revenue, Avg Ticket, No-show %
- Use TanStack Table OR a simpler manual sort if too heavy. TanStack is already in deps, so use it for consistency with Sprint 4.

23	async function fetchClientsData(
24	  supabase: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createClient>>,
25	  studioId: string,
26	  from: string | undefined,
27	  to: string | undefined,
28	): Promise<ClientsKpis> {
29	  const ninetyDaysAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()
30	
31	  // All-time clients + completed bookings (filtered by period if range given)
32	  const [allClients, bookings] = await Promise.all([
33	    supabase.from('clients').select('id, created_at').eq('studio_id', studioId),
34	    supabase.from('bookings')
35	      .select('client_id, studio_id, scheduled_at, price_cents, deposit_cents')
36	      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
37	      .eq('status', 'completed')
38	      .order('scheduled_at', { ascending: true })
39	      .then((r) => {
40	        if (!r.data) return r
41	        let filtered = r.data
42	        if (from) filtered = filtered.filter((b) => b.scheduled_at >= from)
43	        if (to) filtered = filtered.filter((b) => b.scheduled_at <= to)
44	        return { ...r, data: filtered }
45	      }),
46	  ])
47	
48	  if (allClients.error) throw allClients.error
49	  if (bookings.error) throw bookings.error
50	
51	  // Count clients created inside the date window (for "new this period")
52	  const clientsInWindow = (allClients.data ?? []).filter((c) => {
53	    if (from && c.created_at < from) return false
54	    if (to && c.created_at > to) return false
55	    return true
56	  })
57	
58	  const totalClients = clientsInWindow.length
59	
60	  const clientSpend = new Map<string, number>()
61	  const clientLastVisit = new Map<string, string>()
62	
63	  for (const b of bookings.data ?? []) {
64	    if (!b.client_id) continue
65	    const rev = (b.price_cents ?? 0) + (b.deposit_cents ?? 0)
66	    clientSpend.set(b.client_id, (clientSpend.get(b.client_id) ?? 0) + rev)
67	    const prev = clientLastVisit.get(b.client_id)
68	    if (!prev || b.scheduled_at > prev) clientLastVisit.set(b.client_id, b.scheduled_at)
69	  }
70	
71	  const returningClients = Array.from(clientSpend.entries()).filter(([id]) => {
72	    const sessions = (bookings.data ?? []).filter((b) => b.client_id === id).length
73	    return sessions > 1
74	  }).length
75	
76	  const newClients = totalClients - returningClients
77	  const inactiveClients = Array.from(clientLastVisit.entries())
78	    .filter(([, last]) => last < ninetyDaysAgo).length
79	
80	  const ltvValues = Array.from(clientSpend.values()).sort((a, b) => a - b)
81	  const avgLtv = ltvValues.length > 0
82	    ? Math.round(ltvValues.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / ltvValues.length)
83	    : 0
84	
85	  return {
86	    totalClients,
87	    newClients,
88	    returningClients,
89	    inactiveClients,
90	    avgLtv,
91	    retentionRate: totalClients > 0 ? Math.round((returningClients / totalClients) * 100) : 0,
92	  }
93	}

33	async function fetchInventoryData(

35	  studioId: string,
36	  from: string | undefined,
37	  to: string | undefined,
38	): Promise<InventoryBlock> {
39	  const [itemsResult, movementsResult] = await Promise.all([
40	    supabase
41	      .from('inventory_items')
42	      .select('id, name, category, current_stock, min_threshold, cost_per_unit_cents, supplier_id')
43	      .eq('studio_id', studioId),
44	    supabase
45	      .from('inventory_movements')
46	      .select('item_id, qty_delta, reason, created_at, inventory_items(name, cost_per_unit_cents)')
47	      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
48	      .lt('qty_delta', 0) // consumption only
49	      .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
50	      .then((r) => {
51	        if (r.data) {
52	          let filtered = r.data
53	          if (from) filtered = filtered.filter((m) => m.created_at >= from)
54	          if (to) filtered = filtered.filter((m) => m.created_at <= to)
55	          return { ...r, data: filtered }
56	        }
57	        return r
58	      }),
59	  ])
60	
61	  if (itemsResult.error) throw itemsResult.error
62	  if (movementsResult.error) throw movementsResult.error
63	
64	  const items = itemsResult.data ?? []
65	  const movements = movementsResult.data ?? []
66	
67	  // Definition: at or below threshold, and min_threshold is actually set (> 0).
68	  // Must match /api/inventory/stock-alerts directLowStockCount to keep UI counts consistent.
69	  const lowStockCount = items.filter(
70	    (i) => i.min_threshold > 0 && i.current_stock <= i.min_threshold,
71	  ).length
72	
73	  const totalCogsConsumed = movements.reduce((sum, m) => {
74	    const item = m.inventory_items
75	    const cost = Array.isArray(item)
76	      ? (item[0]?.cost_per_unit_cents ?? 0)
77	      : ((item as { cost_per_unit_cents?: number } | null)?.cost_per_unit_cents ?? 0)
78	    return sum + Math.abs(m.qty_delta) * cost
79	  }, 0)
80	
81	  // Stock value = quantity × cost per unit, stored in cents (integer) for consistent 2-decimal formatting
82	  const stockValueCents = items.reduce((sum, i) => {
83	    return sum + i.current_stock * (i.cost_per_unit_cents ?? 0)
84	  }, 0)
85	
86	  // Category breakdown — totalValue in cents (integer)
87	  const categoryMap = items.reduce<Record<string, { count: number; totalValue: number }>>((acc, i) => {
88	    const cat = i.category ?? 'Uncategorized'
89	    if (!acc[cat]) acc[cat] = { count: 0, totalValue: 0 }
90	    acc[cat].count++
91	    acc[cat].totalValue += Math.round(i.current_stock * (i.cost_per_unit_cents ?? 0))
92	    return acc
93	  }, {})
94	
95	  return {
96	    kpis: { totalItems: items.length, lowStockCount, totalCogsConsumed, stockValueCents },
97	    categoryBreakdown: Object.entries(categoryMap).map(([name, d]) => ({ name, ...d })),
98	  }
99	}

4	export const RangeSchema = z.object({

10	export type AnalyticsRange = { from: string; to: string }
11	export type ParsedRange = {
12	  current: AnalyticsRange
13	  prior?: AnalyticsRange
14	  compare: boolean
15	}

17	/** Default date range: last 30 days (today included). */
18	export function defaultLast30(): AnalyticsRange {
19	  const today = new Date()
20	  return {
21	    from: startOfDay(subDays(today, 29)).toISOString(),
22	    to: endOfDay(today).toISOString(),
23	  }
24	}

26	/**
27	 * Parse from/to/compare out of URL search params (or a plain object).
28	 * Falls back to last-30d when from/to are absent or invalid.
29	 */
30	export function parseRange(
31	  searchParams: URLSearchParams | Record<string, string | undefined>,
32	): ParsedRange {
33	  const raw =
34	    searchParams instanceof URLSearchParams
35	      ? Object.fromEntries(searchParams.entries())
36	      : searchParams
37	
38	  const parsed = RangeSchema.safeParse(raw)
39	  const data = parsed.success ? parsed.data : { from: undefined, to: undefined, compare: '0' as const }
40	
41	  const fallback = defaultLast30()
42	  const current: AnalyticsRange = {
43	    from: data.from ?? fallback.from,
44	    to: data.to ?? fallback.to,
45	  }
46	  const compare = data.compare === '1'
47	
48	  const out: ParsedRange = { current, compare }
49	  if (compare) out.prior = priorRange(current)
50	  return out
51	}

53	/**
54	 * Given a range, return the equal-length window immediately before it.
55	 * E.g. Apr 1–30 → Mar 1–31 (30d prior).
56	 */
57	export function priorRange(r: AnalyticsRange): AnalyticsRange {
58	  const days = rangeDays(r)
59	  const fromDate = new Date(r.from)
60	  const toDate = new Date(r.to)
61	  return {
62	    from: startOfDay(subDays(fromDate, days)).toISOString(),
63	    to: endOfDay(subDays(toDate, days)).toISOString(),
64	  }
65	}

67	/** Number of calendar days the range spans (inclusive). */
68	export function rangeDays(r: AnalyticsRange): number {
69	  const diff = differenceInCalendarDays(new Date(r.to), new Date(r.from))
